title: Feature Raft — cheap routing for token-frugal responses
content:
What if we had a tiny, consensus-y routing layer (Feature Raft) that makes per-request routing decisions to favor low-cost model variants without adding user-visible latency?

Goal / Problem
- Many customers want better unit economics but are nervous about quality regressions.
- Current approach: static routing rules (by API key / route) + manual canaries. Not flexible enough to opportunistically route short/simple requests to cheaper quantized/ distilled variants.
- Opportunity: fine-grained, request-level routing that considers request entropy, user SLA, cost tier, and recent quality telemetry to pick the cheapest compatible model variant.

High-level idea
- Add a lightweight routing service per-region (small fleet) that has a shared view (eventual) of model variant health and cost profiles.
- On each incoming request, use a quick heuristic/feature extractor to score compatibility with cheaper variants (e.g., prompt length, token budget, deterministic flags, user tier). If score passes threshold, route to cheaper variant; otherwise route to primary model.
- Continuously run micro-evals on sampling of responses and feed back a confidence score for routing decisions.

Why this is different / valuable
- Dynamic and automated: reacts to model drift and quality regressions faster than static config.
- Transparent to devs (pluggable toggle per-route) and auditable (we log which variant served which request).
- Can substantially reduce per-token costs for chat-heavy customers where many turns are short/simple.

Quick user stories
- As a product engineer, I want route-level opt-in so I can enable frugal routing for non-critical assistant endpoints.
- As an SRE, I want to see how many requests were diverted to cheaper variants and rollback quickly if quality drops.
- As a finance-owner, I want an estimate of cost-savings after enabling Feature Raft for a route.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Config toggle on route: off / experimental / enforced.
- Heuristic scoring: (prompt tokens < 80 AND user-specified max_latency > 300ms) -> candidate for cheap variant. Simple rules engine implementation.
- Variant selection API: returns model id + expected token-cost multiplier.
- Logging: route_id, request_id, selected_variant, pre/post micro-eval score. Stored in console for 90d.
- Rollback: auto-disable routing when micro-eval failure rate exceeds threshold for 15m.

Telemetry & micro-evals
- Sampling: 0.5% of diverted requests are shadowed to the primary model for quality checks (asynchronous).
- Metrics: per-route diversion_rate, shadow-disagreement-rate, avg_latency_by_variant, cost-savings-estimate.

API / SDK surface (sketch)
- route config: {frugal_routing: {mode: experimental, sample_rate: 0.005, thresholds: {prompt_tokens: 80, max_latency: 300}}} (stored in console / API).
- trace: response headers include X-Redwood-Variant: rwd-quant-7b, X-Redwood-Routing-Score: 0.72 for debugging.

Operational concerns / constraints
- Consistency model: eventual is fine; we only need to converge on variant health/rolling windows. Use small vector clock or simple leader-per-region to avoid split-brain complexity initially.
- Security & compliance: audited logs, customers can opt-out (enterprise requirement).
- Latency budget: routing decision must be <5ms on avg. Keep feature extractor tiny (token counts, route metadata, flags).
- Cost of running the routing fleet should be negligible relative to model costs (use tiny instances, co-locate with load balancers).

Experiment plan (first 6 weeks)
Week 1: Prototype rule engine and trace headers in staging. Wire basic console toggle.
Week 2: Implement diversion logic + simple micro-eval shadowing. Start with single internal route (assistant-slim).
Week 3: Run internal dogfood for 1 team; capture metrics and manual inspection.
Week 4: Open experimental opt-in to 3 external customers (low-risk) with explicit consent.
Week 5: Measure cost delta and shadow disagreement; iterate thresholds.
Week 6: Decide go/no-go for beta wider rollout.

Open questions / risks
- How to quantify acceptable quality degradation? Need product owners to define per-route SLOs for emerging features.
- Is sampling shadowing enough, or do we need synthetic micro-eval suites for each important prompt set? (probably both)
- Interaction with Dedicated / Private deployments: customers may want this locally — design extension points in architecture.
- Legal: need to ensure diverted variant does not cause data residency issues.

Back-of-envelope savings example
- Route sees 50M tokens/month at $0.0004/token = $20k. If 30% of requests are divertable and cheap variant saves 60% per-token -> saving ~= 0.3 * 0.6 * $20k = $3.6k/month for that route. Multiply across many routes = material.

Minimal infra sketch
- Regional routing service (k8s small-deployment): exposes /select-variant endpoint, keeps rolling window stats for variants.
- Control-plane: console toggles + thresholds -> update routing service via config push.
- Shadowing worker: forwards copies to primary async and records disagreement metric.

Next steps (immediate)
- [ ] Sync with Ravi on console UX for toggles + exposure limits (JIRA INF-821 assigned).
- [ ] Spike: implement /select-variant hook and trace headers (owner: me) by 2025-11-22.
- [ ] Draft short comms for customer pilot and risk checklist.

Notes to self
- Keep the heuristics explainable so customers trust us.
- Start conservative: under-divert early, tune up.
- Remember to add audit view in console (who flipped the toggle + when).

Slack refs / links to re-check
- #serving-runtime thread from Oct-Nov (pins: experiment results for rwd-quant-7b).
- GH PR above includes a small PoC of routing headers (PR 2476).

Rough UX copy for console toggle (brain dump)
- Title: Frugal routing (Feature Raft)
- Subtitle: Automatically route low-cost requests to cheaper model variants while guarding quality with shadowing and micro-evals.
- Controls: Mode (Off / Experimental / Enforced), Sample rate for shadowing, Token threshold, Auto-disable window, Contact for pilot.

Long-term ideas (if MVP works)
- ML-based router that learns diversion policy per-route (feature extractor -> small classifier).
- Marketplace-like model-tier scoring so customers can pick different cost/quality tradeoffs for subsets of users.
- Push policies down to Dedicated / Private with local controller and metrics sync (privacy-preserving).

End of draft.

-- jena
